source.title: A single standard for memory: the case for reconsolidation.

confidence_rationale: Strong NRN review arguing memory is a principally DYNAMIC, reconstructive process: consolidated memories re-enter transient instability on reactivation and must re-stabilise. Directly grounds the contested state and the fallible-operator premise (re-stabilisation can alter content). The 6-state labels and allocation policy remain REE overlays, so fidelity is held below ceiling.
failure_signatures: If post-retrieval restabilisation can alter a memory's content, then a 'consolidated' state cannot be treated as immutable ground truth -- any lifecycle store that reads consolidated traces as authoritative-and-final inherits the risk that the trace was silently rewritten during a prior reconsolidation episode.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Consolidated memories can re-enter states of transient instability following reactivation, from which they must again stabilise to persist; the same operational evidence underpins both consolidation and reconsolidation, so memory is principally a dynamic rather than a write-once process.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds two things MECH-391's lifecycle store needs: (1) the 'contested' state (reactivation -> instability -> required re-stabilisation), and (2) the fallible-operator premise that motivates the whole memory_lifecycle_v4 cluster -- if re-stabilisation can change content, memory operators are corruptible and the store must track provenance, not just hold a settled value.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Nader & Hardt establish memory as dynamic/reconstructive; they do not enumerate REE's discrete states nor describe an allocation/integration POLICY. The grounding is for the corrigible, re-writable nature of stored traces, not for the specific control logic MECH-391 adds.
mapping.source_context: Review unifying the operational definitions of consolidation and reconsolidation across rodent and human work.

confidence_components.notes: Supports: the reconstructive/dynamic nature is strongly grounded; fidelity held below ceiling because labels + policy are REE additions.
